sites.source: The BLM page and BLM's RIDB record give no site count or length. The stored 30 ft was derived from note prose that rests only on directory listings (Outdoorsy says 35 ft), so it is cleared. Read 2026-10-28.

facilities.source: https://www.blm.gov/visit/cochetopa-creek-rec-site ('developed campsites and picnic areas located along the creek'; 'Restrooms and Shelters are ADA accessible.'). The stored vault toilets / no water were derived from directory-based note prose and are cleared. Read 2026-10-28.

note: BLM Gunnison Field Office recreation site in Cochetopa Canyon along CO-114 near mile marker 113, between Gunnison and Saguache: developed campsites and picnic areas strung over a ~4-mi stretch on both sides of the highway along Cochetopa Creek, in a steep, rocky canyon. High elevation (~8,700 ft), practically a summer/fall site. --Claude
summary: BLM page + BLM's RIDB record: free ('No Fee'), not reservable, 14-day limit, phone (970) 642-4940 matches. BLM describes 'developed campsites and picnic areas located along the creek' over 'a 4 mile stretch along both sides of State Highway 114 near mile marker 113', with ADA restrooms and shelters, but publishes no site count, layout or lengths. Cleared directory-derived max length (30), hookups, vault-toilet and no-water values. Note rewritten from BLM's own description; the pull-off count and field facts dropped.
flags: INCLUSION (for AWH): BLM's own page calls these 'developed campsites and picnic areas located along the creek' with 'Restrooms and Shelters' - so the agency does designate developed campsites, not just a parking allowance - but it publishes no count, map, site numbers or lengths, and the area is 'a 4 mile stretch along both sides of State Highway 114'. On imagery at the pin (z18) only the highway, a dirt track junction and the creek show; no table/fire-ring site layout could be identified there. Directory listings (Outdoorsy: 'up to 15 sites', RVs to ~35 ft; Campendium: dry camping) are the only source for the size. Keep or drop is a human call; nothing here fails the criteria outright.
Pin 38.30606,-106.76426 sits on CO-114 at a dirt-track junction (BLM's RIDB point 38.30625,-106.76442 is ~25 m away). With no per-site data the pin could not be moved onto a site.
Waterfront 'creekside' rests on BLM's 'campsites ... located along the creek' only; no site was located on imagery to measure, so it remains unaudited against the open-apron rule.
Max rig length: no agency figure. Stored 30 ft (cleared) came from directories; Outdoorsy says 35 ft.
